output.summary: Consolidated 94 inline occurrences of the cancelled/rejected/cancelled_weather status triple (90 array-literal call sites + 1 declaration + 4 chained-=== call sites — ticket estimated 'roughly ten') into one top-of-file constant ACCT_EXCLUDED_STATES (renamed from the misleadingly-named ACCT_PAID_STATES, and hoisted from mid-file to the very first <script> block so it is safely visible to code that runs at document-parse time). Added tools/check-excluded-states.mjs, a standalone guard script (not wired into package.json/.github, per scope) that detects both array-literal and chained-comparison duplicates of the triple in any order, and correctly ignores subset/superset variants.

decisions: Hoisted the single ACCT_EXCLUDED_STATES declaration to the very top of the file (before the first IIFE, in the first of 8 <script> blocks) instead of leaving it mid-file where ACCT_PAID_STATES used to live, because earlier <script> blocks contain code (e.g. the SSE/health-check IIFE) that executes immediately at parse time and references the triple — a mid-file const would not exist yet when that code runs. Verified by mapping all real <script> boundaries and confirming with a whole-file node --check pass.

Converted the 4 chained-=== sites (same 3 values, OR'd equality checks instead of an array literal) to ACCT_EXCLUDED_STATES.includes(...) since this is provably behavior-identical and is the same category of literal duplication the ticket targets, just a different syntactic shape; the new guard also detects this shape.

Left all sites whose literal set is not exactly {cancelled, rejected, cancelled_weather} completely unchanged (2-element excludes-rejected variant, 9 sites; 4-element adds-completed variant, 2 sites) and reported them as findings rather than silently normalizing, per explicit task instruction.

Built tools/check-excluded-states.mjs as a zero-dependency, standalone script (node:fs/path/url only) and did not add it to package.json or .github/workflows/**, since this worker owns neither file; that wiring is declared as a follow-up dependency.
risks: The guard matches by permutation of the 3 known literal string values; if the status strings themselves are ever renamed, the guard silently stops catching duplicates until updated — inherent to a grep-based (non-AST) check.
The guard is not wired into any CI gate yet, so it only protects the codebase when run manually until its owning team wires it in.

No live/browser verification against real booking data was possible in this sandbox; verification is limited to static/syntactic checks and a behavioral argument (identical .includes/.indexOf/chained-=== semantics).
dependencies: Wiring tools/check-excluded-states.mjs into package.json (npm script) and/or a .github/workflows/*.yml CI step — deferred to whoever owns those files, since this worker's scope explicitly excludes them.

LAM-31's planned global rename rebase on top of this task and LAM-29 — no action needed from this task beyond staying out of LAM-29's three load-condition sites, which it did (this task only touched status-triple call sites, none of which are Array.isArray(d.sb_...) load conditions).

Consider a documented 'excludes-rejected' 2-element constant for the 9 sites using {cancelled, cancelled_weather} only, if that pattern is judged worth consolidating too.
